source: KICD Mathematical Activities, First Published in 2017; Revised 2024 (text layer)
status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

learning_experiences: collect different types of safe objects from the immediate environment,
group objects according to attributes such as size, colour, use, shape, and texture,
in teams, pair objects with similar attributes such as size, colour, use, shape, and texture,
arrange objects according to size from smallest to biggest and from biggest to smallest,
make patterns of different shapes and sizes using real objects,
assist in arranging items like fruits and cereals, for example beans, maize, and rice according to size, colour, shape and storage at home.
sub_strands.core_competences:
Creativity: learner makes patterns of different shapes and sizes using real objects.
Self-efficacy: learner assists in arranging items according to size, colour, shape, and storage at home.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: in teams, learner matches objects according to size, colour, and shape.
Responsibility: learner assists in arranging items according to size, colour, shape, and storage at home.
sub_strands.pcis:
Safety: learner observes safety as they collect objects from the immediate environment.
Social Cohesion: learner works with peers as they pair and match objects according to size, colour and shape.
sub_strands.links: The learner can relate the skills used in creating patterns to the concept of patterns in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: sort objects according to similar attributes in different situations
match objects with similar attributes in the environment
order objects according to given criteria in different situations
create patterns of different sizes and shapes using real objects
appreciate the use of sorting and grouping items in day-to-day activities

content_topics: Reading and writing numbers in symbols and words
learning_experiences: collect concrete objects from the immediate environment to use in counting activities,
count by 1’s and 2’s up to 20 starting from any point using concrete objects such as number cards, as well as body parts,
take turns in counting numbers forward up to 50,
count numbers backward from 30,
play games that involve representing numbers 1 to 30 using concrete objects,
read and write numbers 1 to 50 in symbols,
practise writing numbers 1 to 10 in words,
fill in missing numbers in number patterns up to 20,
create patterns with numbers up to 20 and share them with other groups,
play games involving whole numbers using digital devices or other resources.
key_inquiry_questions: In what ways can we count from 1 to 20?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital Literacy: learner uses digital devices to play games involving numbers 1 to 50.
Creativity: learner creates patterns with numbers up to 20.
sub_strands.values: Respect: learner appreciates peers as they take turns in counting numbers forward up to 50.
sub_strands.pcis:
Social Cohesion: learner takes turns counting numbers forward up to 50.
Environmental Safety: learner observes safety when collecting concrete objects from the immediate environment.
sub_strands.links:
The learner can relate the skills used in the concept of reading and writing numbers in words and symbols to functional reading and writing in English Language Activities.
The learner can relate the skills used in creating number patterns to the concept of patterns in Creative Activities.

outcomes.text: count numbers forward up to 50
count numbers backward from 30
represent numbers 1 to 30 using concrete objects
read and write numbers 1 to 50 in symbols
read and write numbers 1 to 10 in words
identify missing numbers in number patterns up to 20
appreciate number patterns by creating and extending patterns during play activities

learning_experiences: safely put two groups of objects together and count to get the total,
create scenarios where addition is relevant i.e there are two apples on the table, add three more, how many apples are there,
use flashcards with addition problems to practise quick recall of basic facts,
roll dice to add numbers together,
use number cards or abacus to add a 2-digit number to a 1-digit number without regrouping horizontally and vertically with a sum not exceeding 50,
make number patterns involving addition with numbers up to 50,
play games involving addition using digital devices and other resources.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you add a 2-digit number to a 1-digit number?

add 2 single-digit numbers in different situations
add 3 single-digit numbers in different contexts

learning_experiences: model subtraction using concrete objects,
use ' - ' and '=' signs in writing subtraction sentences,
subtract by counting backward,
subtract using concrete objects,
make subtraction sentences related to basic addition facts,
use number cards or charts safely to work out subtraction of a 1-digit number from a 2-digit number,
work with peers to create patterns involving subtraction.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you subtract a one-digit number from a two-digit number?

outcomes.text: model subtraction as 'taking away' using concrete objects
use the ' - ' and '='signs in writing subtraction sentences
subtract single digit numbers
subtract a 1-digit number from a 2-digit number without regrouping
work out missing numbers in patterns involving subtraction of whole numbers up to 50
play games involving subtraction using digital devices and other resources

learning_experiences: collect objects of different lengths from the immediate environment,
compare objects directly to identify objects that are longer than, shorter than or the same as other objects,
in teams, measure lengths using arbitrary units such as hand spans or walking steps and discuss the measurements,
use arbitrary units to measure the length of different objects in their immediate environment.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you compare the length of two objects?
What can be used to measure the length of the teacher’s table?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: learner measures the length of different objects in their immediate environment.
Communication and collaboration: learner takes turns measuring the length of objects using arbitrary units.
sub_strands.values: Responsibility: learner takes care of objects collected from the environment for learning.
sub_strands.pcis: Social Cohesion: learner works harmoniously in teams as they measure lengths using arbitrary units.
sub_strands.links: The learner can relate the concept of using objects from the environment for learning to the concept of resources in the environment in Environmental Activities.

outcomes.text: collect objects of different lengths from the immediate environment
compare the length of objects using longer than, shorter than, and same as
measure length using arbitrary units
appreciate measuring length using arbitrary units

learning_experiences: collect safe objects of different mass from their immediate environment,
in turn, use safe objects to identify those heavier than, lighter than, or same as,
use an identified empty container of known mass to measure the mass of other objects such as mass of beans, maize or flour as accurately as possible,
play games involving mass using digital devices.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you compare the mass of two or more objects?
How can you show that an object is heavier than, lighter than, or the same as your mathematics textbook?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: learner discusses objects that are heavier, lighter, or have the same mass.
Digital Literacy: learner uses digital devices to play games involving mass.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: learner appreciates the effort of others as they measure the mass of different items.
Respect: learner gives others equal opportunity as they use safe objects to identify heavier, lighter, or objects of the same mass.
sub_strands.pcis:
Safety issues: learner observes safety as they collect objects of different mass from their immediate environment.
Effective communication: learner listens and contributes to discussions on objects that are heavier, lighter, or have the same mass.
sub_strands.links: The learner can relate the concept of safe objects from the environment to the concept of safety in the school environment in Environmental Activities.

outcomes.text: collect objects with different masses from the immediate environment
compare the mass of two objects using heavier than, lighter than, or same as
measure mass using arbitrary units
appreciate measuring mass using arbitrary units in the environment

learning_experiences: collect safe containers of different sizes from the environment,
empty and fill water in different containers to establish which holds more, which holds less, and which holds the same,
jointly fill basins with water using different small containers. The learners to count the number of small containers they use to fill the basin,
re-use containers of different capacities at home and school to keep items.
key_inquiry_questions: How can we find out which of two containers holds more, less, or same as?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to Learn: learner determines the capacity of containers by filling bigger containers with water basins from smaller containers.
Problem-solving: learner reuses containers of different capacities at home and school.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: learner re-uses containers to keep items at home and school.
Unity: learner jointly with others fills bigger containers with water using different small containers.
sub_strands.pcis:
Safety issues: learner collects safe containers of different sizes from the environment.
Sustainable consumption: learner reuses of containers at home and school.
sub_strands.links: The learner can relate the skill of reusing empty containers to the skills of waste management in Environmental Activities.

outcomes.text: collect containers of different capacities from the immediate environment
compare the capacity of two containers using more than, less than, and same as
measure capacity using arbitrary units
re-use empty containers of different capacities to keep items

learning_experiences: sing songs/ rhymes related to days of the week,
tell and write days of the week the way they follow each other,
name activities that take place during the days of the week such as raising flag on Monday and Friday,
sing songs/rhymes related to the months of the year,
discuss and tell their birth month to peers.
key_inquiry_questions: Which day of the week do you raise the school flag?
Which day of the week do you worship?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Self-efficacy: learner confidently sings songs/ rhymes related to days of the week.
Communication and Collaboration: learner discusses and tells his/her birth month to peers.
sub_strands.values:
Peace: learner harmoniously sings songs/ rhymes related to days of the week together.
Patriotism: learner is aware of his/her own culture as they name activities that take place during the days of the week.
sub_strands.pcis:
Citizenship: learner names activities that take place during the days of the week such as raising of the flag.
Social Cohesion: learner collaboratively sings songs/ rhymes related to days of the week together.
sub_strands.links: The learner can relate the concept of time to the concept of weather and the sky, and day and night in Environmental Activities.

outcomes.text: identify days of the week
relate days of the week to various activities
identify months of the year
appreciate activities that are done on different days of the week

learning_experiences: recognise and sort out different Kenyan currency coins sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, and sh.40 according to their value,
recognise a sh.50 note and tell its value,
tell how many coins of sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, sh. 40 by counting,
discuss the price of items in the model classroom shop up to sh.50,
role play buying up to 2 items from the model classroom shop without balance.
key_inquiry_questions: How can you identify Kenyan currency coins and notes?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Citizenship: learner recognises and sorts out different Kenyan currency coins and notes according to their value.
Self-efficacy: learner role plays buying up to 2 items from the model classroom shop.
sub_strands.values:
Integrity: learner displays honesty as they role play selling and buying of items from the model classroom shop.
Patriotism: learner is aware of own culture as they recognise different Kenyan currency coins and notes.
sub_strands.pcis: Financial literacy: learner recognises and sorts out different Kenyan currency coins according to their value.
sub_strands.links: The learner can relate the skill of using money to the concept of our market in Environmental Activities.

outcomes.text: identify Kenyan currency coins
identify the sh.50 Kenyan currency note
count Kenyan currency coins one at a time
use money to buy up to 2 items without balance
appreciate the use of money in buying items from shops

learning_experiences: stand behind one another facing the same side and identify what they have formed as a straight line,
in teams, mark two points on the ground and use a stick to join the two points to make a straight line,
practise drawing straight lines on the ground and in their books,
in teams, form a semicircle, draw a line around it and identify the line drawn as a curved line,
practise drawing curved lines on the ground and in their books,
observe and name lines from different objects in the environment.
key_inquiry_questions: How do you make a line?
sub_strands.values:
Respect: learner appreciates the effort of peers as they work in teams to observe and identify lines from different objects in the environment.
Responsibility: learner follows instructions as they stand behind one another facing the same side to form a straight line.
sub_strands.pcis:
Social Cohesion: learner works harmoniously in teams as they draw straight and curved lines.
Environmental Awareness: learner observes and names lines from different objects in the environment.
sub_strands.links: The learner can relate the concept of drawing straight and curved lines to the concept of drawing in Creative Activities.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: competencies: heading on the page but no text read; a line on this page ran across two columns and was cut by position.

outcomes.text: identify straight lines in different situations
draw straight lines on different surfaces
identify curved lines in different situations
draw curved lines on different surfaces
recognise straight and curved lines from real objects in the environment

learning_experiences: use safe objects from the environment to recognise different shapes such as rectangles, triangles, circles, and oval,
make patterns of their choice using the three shapes,
make patterns, colour them and share with classmates.
key_inquiry_questions: What shapes can you identify in your class?
sub_strands.values:
Peace: learner displays tolerance as they make patterns, colour them and share with classmates.
Responsibility: learner is committed to duty as they work individually to make patterns of their choice using shapes.
sub_strands.pcis:
Safety in the learning environment: learner uses safe objects from the environment for learning.
Creative thinking: learner makes patterns of their choice using shapes.
sub_strands.links:
The learner can relate the skills used in making and colouring patterns to drawing and decoration skills in Creative Activities.
The learner can relate the concept of using safe objects from the environment to the concept of safety in the school environmental in Environmental Activities.

outcomes.text: identify rectangles, triangles, and circles in objects from the environment
make patterns involving rectangles, triangles, circles, and ovals
appreciate the beauty of patterns in different fabrics

indicators.indicator: Ability to sort, group, and match objects according to similar attributes (size, shape, colour, use, texture).

levels.EE: The learner sorts, groups, and matches objects according to five attributes systematically and correctly.
levels.ME: The learner sorts, groups and matches objects according to five attributes correctly.
levels.AE: The learner sorts and groups or matches objects according to any three to four attributes correctly.
levels.BE: The learner sorts, groups or matches objects according to any two attributes partially correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to create patterns by ordering objects and numbers according to different criteria (addition, subtraction, size, shape, colour).

levels.EE: The learner creates patterns by ordering objects and numbers according to five different criteria systematically and correctly.
levels.ME: The learner creates patterns by ordering objects and numbers according to five different criteria correctly.
levels.AE: The learner creates patterns by ordering objects or numbers according to any three or four different criteria correctly.
levels.BE: The learner creates patterns by ordering objects or numbers according to any two different criteria partially correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to count numbers forward up to 50 and backward from 30.

levels.EE: The learner counts numbers forward up to 50 and backward from 30, correctly and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner counts numbers forward up to 50 and backward from 30 correctly.
levels.AE: The learner counts numbers forward up to 40 or backward from 20 correctly.
levels.BE: The learner counts numbers forward up to 30 and backward from 10 partially correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to read and write numbers 1 to 50 in symbols and numbers 1 to 10 in words.

levels.EE: The learner reads and writes numbers 1 to 50 in symbols and 1 to 10 in words correctly and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner reads and writes numbers 1 to 50 in symbols and 1 to 10 in words correctly.
levels.AE: The learner reads and/or writes numbers 1 to 40 in symbols and/or 1 to 10 in words correctly.
levels.BE: The learner reads and/or writes numbers 1 to 30 in symbols and/or 1 to 5 in words partially correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify missing numbers in number patterns up to 20.

levels.EE: The learner identifies missing numbers in number patterns up to 20 correctly and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner identifies missing numbers in number patterns up to 20 correctly.
levels.AE: The learner identifies missing numbers in number patterns up to 15 correctly.
levels.BE: The learner identifies missing numbers in number patterns up to 10 partially correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to add a 2-digit number to a 1-digit number without regrouping with a sum not exceeding 50.

levels.EE: The learner adds a 2-digit number to a 1-digit number without regrouping with a sum not exceeding 50 correctly and systematically.
levels.ME: The learner adds a 2- digit number to a 1- digit number without regrouping with a sum not exceeding 50 correctly.
levels.AE: The learner adds a 2- digit number to a 1- digit number without regrouping with a sum not exceeding 30 correctly.
levels.BE: The learner adds a 2- digit number to a 1- digit number without regrouping with a sum not exceeding 20 correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to subtract a 1- digit number from a 2- digit number up to 50 without regrouping.

levels.EE: The learner subtracts a 1- digit number from a 2- digit number up to 50 without regrouping correctly and systematically.
levels.ME: The learner subtracts a 1-digit number from a 2-digit number up to 50 without regrouping correctly.
levels.AE: The learner subtracts a 1-digit number from a 2-digit number up to 30 without regrouping correctly.
levels.BE: The learner subtracts a 1-digit number from a 2-digit number up to 20 without regrouping correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to work out missing numbers in patterns involving the addition and subtraction of whole numbers up to 50.

levels.EE: The learner works out missing numbers in patterns involving the addition and subtraction of whole numbers up to 50 correctly and systematically.
levels.ME: The learner works out missing numbers in patterns involving the addition and subtraction of whole numbers up to 50 correctly.
levels.AE: The learner works out missing numbers in patterns involving the addition or subtraction of whole numbers up to 40 correctly.
levels.BE: The learner works out missing numbers in patterns involving the addition or subtraction of whole numbers up to 20 correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to compare lengths of objects using longer than, shorter than and same as.

levels.EE: The learner compares lengths of objects using longer than, shorter than, and same as accurately and comprehensively.
levels.ME: The learner compares lengths of objects using longer than, shorter than, and same as accurately.
levels.AE: The learner compares lengths of objects using any two of; longer than, shorter than, or same as accurately.
levels.BE: The learner compares lengths of objects using any one of; longer than, shorter than, or same as.

indicators.indicator: Ability to compare mass of two objects using heavier than, lighter than and same as.

levels.EE: The learner compares the mass of two objects using heavier than, lighter than and same as accurately and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner compares the mass of two objects using heavier than, lighter than and same as accurately.
levels.AE: The learner compares the mass of two objects using any two of; heavier than, lighter than or same as accurately.
levels.BE: The learner compares the mass of two objects using any one of; heavier than, lighter than or same as.

indicators.indicator: Ability to compare the capacity of two containers using more than, less than, and same as.

levels.EE: The learner compares the capacity of two containers using more than, less than, and same as accurately and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner compares the capacity of two containers using more than, less than, and same as accurately.
levels.AE: The learner compares the capacity of two containers using any of two; more than, less than, and same as accurately.
levels.BE: The learner compares the capacity of two containers using any one of; more than, less than and same as.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify and relate days of the week to various activities.

levels.EE: The learner identifies and relates the days of the week to various activities correctly and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner identifies and relates the days of the week to various activities correctly.
levels.AE: The learner identifies and relates some days of the week to various activities accurately.
levels.BE: The learner identifies some days of the week.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify months of the year.

levels.EE: The learner identifies 12 months of the year correctly and in sequence.
levels.ME: The learner identifies 12 months of the year correctly.
levels.AE: The learner identifies at most 7 months of the year correctly.
levels.BE: The learner identifies at most 4 months of the year correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify Kenyan currency coins sh.1, sh. 5, sh.10, sh. 20, sh. 40, and sh. 50 note.

levels.EE: The learner identifies Kenyan currency coins sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, sh.40, and sh.50 note correctly and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner identifies Kenyan currency coins sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, sh.40, and sh.50 note correctly.
levels.AE: The learner identifies at least 4 of Kenyan currency coins sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, sh.40, or sh.50 note accurately.
levels.BE: The learner identifies at least 2 of Kenyan currency coins sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, or sh.40.

indicators.indicator: Ability to count currency coins of sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, and sh.40 one at a time.

levels.EE: The learner counts currency coins of sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, and sh.40 one at a time accurately and fluently.
levels.ME: The learner counts currency coins of sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, and sh.40 one at a time accurately.
levels.AE: The learner counts at least 4 currency coins of sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, and sh.40 one at a time accurately.
levels.BE: The learner counts at least 2 currency coins of sh.1, sh.5, sh.10, sh.20, and sh.40 one at a time.

indicators.indicator: Ability to draw straight and curved lines.

levels.EE: The learner draws straight and curved lines accurately and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner draws straight and curved lines accurately.
levels.AE: The learner draws straight and curved lines partially accurately.
levels.BE: The learner draws straight or curved lines partially accurately.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify shapes in an object (rectangles, triangles, circles, ovals).

levels.EE: The learner identifies four shapes in an object correctly and names them.
levels.ME: The learner identifies four shapes in an object correctly.
levels.AE: The learner identifies any three shapes in an object correctly.
levels.BE: The learner identifies any two shapes in an object.

indicators.indicator: Ability to make patterns involving three shapes (rectangles, triangles, circles, ovals).

levels.EE: The learner makes patterns involving four shapes accurately and consistently.
levels.ME: The learner makes patterns involving four shapes accurately.
levels.AE: The learner makes patterns involving any three shapes accurately.
levels.BE: The learner makes patterns involving any two shapes.
